articles.headline: Erik ten Hag on former Man United legends' criticism: 'They could help the club and players more'
articles.description: Former Manchester United head coach Erik ten Hag has spoken candidly about the impact that the criticism of former club legends has on the club and current players.
articles.headlineJa: エリック・テン・ハフ、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのレジェンドたちによる批判について：「彼らはもっとクラブや選手を助けることができるはずだ」
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの元監督エリック・テン・ハフが、クラブのレジェンドたちによる批判がクラブや現役選手に与える影響について率直に語った。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United head coach Erik ten Hag has spoken candidly about the impact that the criticism of former club legends has on the club and current players.

In the second part of an interview with The Athletic, -- the first part in which he had said that Cristiano Ronaldo "let United down" during his second spell at the club -- Ten Hag said that pundits who often commented on the events at United, sometimes with harsh words, were part of the club's history and "do not always know what's going on."

"It's everywhere the same; they always want to protect their legacies," the ex-Ajax head coach said. "It's no different than Bayern Munich or Ajax; they do the same. But they are [part of United's] history, and they do not always know what's going on. Football evolves.

"For United, it's clear: they had great contributions, they achieved massive results, trophies for the club and for themselves, so I respect them."

Former United players -- who were all part of the hugely successful Sir Alex Ferguson era -- that regularly pass comment on the club include Gary Neville, Roy Keane, Wayne Rooney, Rio Ferdinand and Paul Scholes.

Neville hosts The Overlap podcast, while Keane is part of its permanent panel. They are both regular pundits on Sky Sports and have been known to sharply criticise United in recent years.

Keane labelled the club a "circus" following Lisandro Martínez's outburst that slammed the club hierarchy, after a defeat to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League.

"They're obviously not together," Keane said on The Overlap's Stick to Football podcast. "It is chaotic there from the top to the bottom. We go there on match days and I don't like the feeling around the club.

"It just seems chaotic -- statements can reflect it. It was chaotic with how they got to [Michael] Carrick as their manager.

"We said from day one there were better options out there, and maybe the players are looking at there's better options as players out there. It's chaos, it's like a circus."

In September, Neville branded United's second-half display against Fulham in a 1-1 draw as the "worst 15 minutes" he's ever seen a United team play.

Ten Hag said that some United players would get irritated with the commentary by former club heroes but also claimed that he himself had a good relationship with the pundits.

- Martínez's Man United outburst begs the question: Why do Premier League executives stay silent?

- Michael Carrick: I feel backing of Man United board but need to win games

- Cesc Fàbregas calls suggestions he could replace Michael Carrick at Man United disrespectful

"I have to say, I had a very good relationship with them all, with Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand. I did nice interviews with them both, so it didn't hurt me. Of course, they have podcasts, they have their models. Sometimes it's difficult for players. Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it.

"They achieved massive successes. But also, they can help the club more, help the play

articles.headline: Anthony Gordon: PSG had better moments, more quality in Barcelona win
articles.description: Anthony Gordon has offered an honest appraisal of Barcelona's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, saying the European champions had "better moments and more quality."
articles.headlineJa: アンソニー・ゴードン：バルセロナ戦の勝利において、PSGはより良い局面を作り出し、質が高かった
articles.descriptionJa: アンソニー・ゴードンは、バルセロナがパリ・サンジェルマンに2-4で敗れた試合について率直な評価を下し、欧州チャンピオン（PSG）の方が「より良い場面が多く、質が高かった」と述べた。
articles.body:
Anthony Gordon has offered an honest appraisal of Barcelona's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, saying the European champions had "better moments and more quality."

Barça coach Hansi Flick had challenged his side to show they can compete with the best side in Europe before the match.

Goals from Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal kept Barça in the game but two late strikes from Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz ensured PSG maintained their 100% win record in this season's Champions League.

Gordon praised the French side and said they simply played better for longer.

"I think they deserved it in the end. I feel like they were the better team," Gordon told TNT Sport.

"They had better moments with more quality and I feel like athletically they were able to sustain the pressure, the intensity for longer than we were.

"They've been the team to beat for two years, tonight is a great example of why."

- How Raphinha's latest transformation made him into Barcelona's star striker

- Barcelona, PSG thriller  proves these are the two best in the world

- Ngumoha sparks Liverpool's comeback Champions League win

Gordon said Barça, who had won 11-straight games before Tuesday's defeat, want to emulate PSG, but the result showed there is plenty of room for improvement.

"I think we can take great positives because we played well, it was a competitive spectacle," Gordon said. "But we've still got work to do and I think that's a good position.

"They've been the best for two years, they're still the team to beat and we need to take from this that we need to do enough work, analyse this game and try and become that team. Try and become the team that needs to be beaten."

Barça have the chance to bounce back immediately against Spanish rivals Real Madrid in Sunday's Clasico.

articles.headline: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured his ACL, Paris Saint-Germain confirm
articles.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament injury during Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory against Barcelona.
articles.headlineJa: パリ・サンジェルマンが発表、フヴィチャ・クヴァラツヘリアが前十字靭帯を断裂
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンがチャンピオンズリーグのバルセロナ戦で勝利した際、フヴィチャ・クヴァラツヘリアが前十字靭帯を断裂した。
articles.body:
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to miss to the rest of the 2026-27 season after sustaining a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament injury during Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory against Barcelona.

The 25-year-old, who was injured during a collision with Barceloa's Xavi Espart in the 59th minute of Tuesday's game, had to be carried from the field by PSG medical staff due to the extent of the injury.

And the Champions League winners have now confirmed that the former Napoli player will undergo surgery on his right knee "in the coming days" to repair the injury.

In a statement, PSG said: "Having suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday's match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days."

There is no timescale on the Georgia international's likely return to action, but with such injuries usually leading to at least nine months on the sidelines, Kavaratskhelia's chances of playing again this season are slim.

- Sources: Barcelona report PSG to UEFA for 'aggressive' tifo

- Tired Barcelona undone by 'too many mistakes' as perfect start ends at PSG

- Barcelona, PSG thriller in Champions League proves these are the two best

And in a further blow to PSG's prospects this season, forward Ousmane Dembélé and defender Marquinhos are both facing a "few weeks" out of action after also being injured against Barcelona.

Reigning Ballon d'Or winner Dembele limped off after just 19 minutes with an injury to his left thigh while captain Marquinhos is also now set for a spell on the sidelines with a right thigh problem.

PSG, who consolidated top spot in the Champions League League Phase by beating Barça, travel to Ligue 1 leaders Lyon in a top of the table clash on Sunday.

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama, Giannis Antetokounmpo lead record African heritage presence in NBA
articles.description: Eighteen African countries are represented in the league, with Nigeria accounting for nearly half the number with 29 players of Nigerian origin.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマとヤニス・アデトクンボが牽引、NBAでアフリカ系選手の在籍数が過去最多を記録
articles.descriptionJa: リーグにはアフリカ18カ国の出身者が在籍しており、そのうちナイジェリア系選手が29名と、全体の約半分を占めている。
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, Miami Heat teammates Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, along with Philadelphia 76ers centre Joel Embiid and Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall draft pick, lead a record 67 players of African origin on opening night rosters for the 2026-27 NBA season.

This year's African presence in the league exceeds the more than 55 players born on the continent or with at least one African parent at the start of last season and comes despite the league's overall international contingent falling to 125 from last season's record 135.

In total, the international players represent 43 countries across six continents, with every NBA team carrying at least one international player.

Eighteen African countries are represented in the league, with Nigeria accounting for nearly half the number with 29 players of Nigerian origin.

Besides Adebayo and Antetokounmpo, Nigeria also has OG Anunoby, who helped the New York Knicks to the title last season, Washington Wizards centre Deandre Ayton, whose father is from Nigeria, along with Precious Achiuwa, Charles Bassey, Adem Bona, Josh Okogie, Felix Okpara and Ugonna Onyenso, with Okpara and Onyenso on two-way contracts.

Senegal is a distant second with six, with Cameroon and Mali tied one behind on five. The Senegalese contingent includes Mouhamed Gueye, Khalifa Diop, Tacko Fall, Ousmane Dieng, Sidy Cissoko and Alex Sarr.

Embiid tops the Cameroon posse, alongside Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, New Orleans Pelicans centre Yves Missi, Chicago Bulls Noa Essengue and Orlando Magic guard Noah Penda.

The African presence extends across several other national contingents. Leading the line is France, which has 13 players of African heritage out of their total of 17 players, including Wembanyama and Nolan Traoré.

Wembanyama's family roots are in the Democratic Republic of the Congo through his father, Félix, while Traoré is of Ivorian and Malian heritage. France's contingent also includes Wizards teammates Bilal Coulibaly, who has ties to Mali, and Alex Sarr, who is of Senegalese origin.

Elsewhere, Japan's Rui Hachimura is of Benin heritage through his father Zakari Jamil, Germany's Dennis Schroeder is of Gambin heritage and Portugal's Neemias Queta has ties to Guinea-Bissau.

These are record numbers for the NBA. For the 2023-24 season, the league reported 15 players from Africa and another 35 with at least one parent from an African country for a total of 50.

That number went up in the 2024-25 season, with a record-tying 17 players from the continent, along with 35 more with African parentage for a total of 52.

Tuesday's opening-night tripleheader saw five of these African heritage players take to the court, with Embiid recording 13 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and three blocks as Philadelphia beat defending champion New York 106-100. articles.headline: BAL to confirm franchises in 2027, but no timeline on new structure - Mark Tatum
articles.description: NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum said the league plans to announce BAL franchises in 2027, but there is no timeline for a change in the league format.
articles.headlineJa: マーク・タタム氏、BALは2027年にフランチャイズを確定させるが、新体制のスケジュールは未定と発表
articles.descriptionJa: NBAのマーク・タタム副コミッショナーは、リーグが2027年にBALのフランチャイズを発表する計画である一方、リーグ形式の変更に関するスケジュールは決まっていないと述べた。
articles.body:
NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum has said that the first Basketball Africa League (BAL) franchises will be announced in 2027, but the timeline for a transition to a new structure is still to be determined.

Until now, teams have had to qualify through FIBA's Road to BAL qualifiers, and this would remain an option for non-franchise teams. However, BAL franchises would have recurring automatic participation in the league.

The 2027 season has long been discussed as a transition point from the old model to the new franchise system, but the Road to BAL is proceeding in the meantime.

"We've made significant progress on transitioning the Basketball Africa League to a franchise model," Tatum said.

"Ahead of the initial deadline, which was in June, we received dozens of bids for permanent franchises across all of our target markets, including significant interest from established basketball markets like Nigeria and Senegal. We also saw bids from emerging markets with long-term growth potential like Kenya, Rwanda, and South Africa."

A bid from Cape Town centering around the GrandWest Arena -- led by some of the executives who oversaw the Cape Town Tigers through their run to three successive national titles and the 2024 BAL semi-finals -- was rejected.

One of the execs involved, Cape Town Tigers' founding owner Lari Kangas, told ESPN the Cape Town bid was fully funded. Potential investors into a franchise elsewhere in South Africa remain in discussions. AfroBallers reported that Spike Lee signed a letter of intent to join a bidding group for a franchise in the country.

Meanwhile, Kenya's Nairobi City Thunder have unveiled Lupita Nyong'o as an investor. However, there has still been no announcement of a permanent franchise.

"We're advancing discussions with priority bidders, and plan to announce our first BAL franchises in 2027," Tatum continued.

"What looks like in terms of when those franchises will begin playing in the BAL is still TBD. We're still working through that, but we do expect to introduce BAL franchises into playing in the BAL on a rolling basis.

"Again, the principle there is going to be similar to Europe where we will continue to preserve open spots that clubs across Africa can qualify for on an annual basis. So we'll always have that, and again, this is a partnership with FIBA. We'll always have that pathway for clubs that are not permanent franchises to be able to play into the top tier competition."

The NBA has run the BAL together with FIBA in Africa since the inaugural edition in 2021. The league has yet to reach profitability, but has produced several talented players - notably the Phoenix Suns' Khaman Maluach and the Florida Gators' Rueben Chinyelu.

articles.headline: Martinez's Man United outburst begs the question: Why do Premier League executives stay silent?
articles.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez publicly targeted the club's hierarchy last week. But why do you never hear from senior executives from Premier League clubs?
articles.headlineJa: マルティネスのマンユナイテッドに対する激昂が突きつける問い：なぜプレミアリーグの幹部たちは沈黙を貫くのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのDFリサンドロ・マルティネスが先週、クラブの上層部を公に批判した。しかし、なぜプレミアリーグのクラブの幹部から声明が出ることはないのだろうか。
articles.body:
Lisandro Martínez's extraordinary post-match outburst to Amazon Prime following Manchester United's 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid last week highlighted an arrangement that has served the Premier League's sporting executives rather well: they're influential in picking a club's manager and building the squad, but are nowhere to be seen when the team struggles.

Martínez's comments were an unusually explicit exercise in finger-pointing, and he has since apologized. While players have long criticized their own performances, collective failures or even, occasionally, individual teammates, the manager or head coach has often represented the thinly disguised target.

But Martínez, who has been at the club since 2022, went further: He questioned why United showed a lack of "ambition" in the transfer market and all-but-named director of football Jason Wilcox as the main culprit. "I expect more from our technical director," Martínez said, before asking: "You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas?"

Manager Michael Carrick was spared criticism; instead, the finger was pointed "upstairs." Wilcox's title at United may now be director of football, and no longer technical director following his promotion last year, but he is still responsible for player recruitment and squad construction. As far as Martínez is concerned, Wilcox's office door is where the buck stops.

But beyond whether Martínez's criticism was justified, whether he should have aired it publicly and whether the outburst was premeditated, there are some interesting questions at play. Why did it take a center back to publicly demand answers from a director of football? Should the executives who build Premier League squads also be required to face the media regularly? And why has their absence been accepted for so long?

Note: The terms "manager" and "head coach" have been used casually throughout the piece, but if you want my definition of either role, click here.

The rise of the sporting executive in Europe

Public scrutiny is customary in football, but historically it was always the manager who was left to answer the media's questions about recruitment, strategy, and the club's general direction. When managers like Man United's Sir Alex Ferguson or Arsenal's Arsene Wenger were in control of everything in the 1990s, it made more sense. But now those in charge of matters on the pitch are often disconnected with the commercial, financial, and even recruitment side of things because of the rise of the sporting executive.

The sporting executive was predominantly a continental concept from its origins. Italo Allodi, an early Italian pioneer, began his executive career at Mantova in the mid-1950s, before he went on to build Helenio Herrera's "Grande Inter" team in Milan in 1959.

articles.headline: Tired Barcelona undone by 'too many mistakes' as perfect start ends at PSG
articles.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick says his tired Barcelona side made too many mistakes as their perfect start to the season ended with a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday in the Champions League.
articles.headlineJa: 疲労が見えたバルセロナ、「あまりに多くのミス」に泣く。PSG戦で完璧なスタートに終止符
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナのハンジ・フリック監督は、水曜日に開催されたチャンピオンズリーグのパリ・サンジェルマン戦で4-2で敗れ、今シーズンの完璧なスタートに終わりを告げた要因について、疲労したチームがあまりに多くのミスを犯したためだと述べた。
articles.body:
PARIS -- Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said his tired side made too many mistakes as their perfect start to the season ended with a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday in the Champions League.

Desiré Doué, Lucas Hernández, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz were all on target as PSG edged an enthralling game at the Parc des Princes to make it three wins from three in Europe this season.

Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal had twice drawn Barça level before the Spanish champions conceded twice late on as their 11-game winning run at the start of the new campaign came to an end.

- PSG injuries can't overshadow signature UCL win over Barcelona

- Barcelona, PSG thriller in Champions League proves these are the two best

"I think it was a fantastic game from both teams," Flick said in the post-game news conference. "We made too many mistakes, especially in ball possession, easy ball losses.

"This is what we have to analyse. But I saw a lot of good things also. For me it was a great test for us. You saw today in which areas we have to improve. This is what we will do.

"We have to understand the mistakes happen because [the players] are not fresh. What they had to do the last couple of weeks is unbelievable. I appreciate the attitude. A lot of things were fantastic."

The fixture had been billed as a clash between the best two sides in the world right now: back-to-back European champions PSG taking on a Barça side that had scored 48 goals in their 11 wins this season.

Barcelona's 11-game winning start to the season in all competitions had been tied for the third-longest winning start by a team from Europe's top five leagues and tied for the longest by a Spanish club.

However, Flick lamented Barça's preparation for the match, with their flight back from Seville after beating Real Betis on Saturday cancelled due to storms in Spain.

"Everyone knows what happens after [the Betis win], so it's not the perfect recovery," he added. "It's not an excuse, just for you to understand why maybe we were not at the top level.

"But it was a good level. We have to learn from this game. PSG had a lot of chances -- Joan García was fantastic in goal for us -- but so did we. We have to take them. This is what I saw from PSG today.

"But in October you can't win titles. You win the Champions League in June. This is the way how we want to do it."

Flick also confirmed the surprise decision to start Rodri on the bench was made with Sunday's visit from Real Madrid LaLiga in mind.

Victory in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou would move Barça nine points clear of José Mourinho's side and extend their winning streak in the league to 10 games.

"Yes," Flick said when asked if Rodri, who came on for the final 30 minutes, was reserved for Madrid. "He played a lot of minutes with [Spain] and also the last games with us after the break.

"I spoke with him and told him we make this decision and [Marc] Bernal started. For me, it was a good solution. Hopefully he's fresh on Sunday."

Dani

articles.headline: Sources: Barcelona report PSG to UEFA for 'aggressive' tifo
articles.description: Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：バルセロナが「攻撃的な」ティフォを巡りPSGをUEFAに報告
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のチャンピオンズリーグの試合前にPSGのサポーターが掲げたティフォを巡り、バルセロナがUEFAに報告したと関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.

As the players came on to the pitch before kickoff, fans behind one of the goals at Parc des Princes held up a giant banner which showed a masked figure carrying a chainsaw and destroying the Barça badge.

Underneath were the words: "Massacre, Parisian style."

In addition, pyrotechnics were used to mimic the sparks coming from the chainsaw as it hacked away at the Barça crest.

The source said the imagery evoked was both "overly aggressive and offensive."

On the pitch, PSG ran out 4-2 winners in an entertaining game between two of Europe's most in-form sides.

Desiré Douré, Lucas Hernández, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz were all on target as PSG made it three wins out of three in the Champions League this season.

For Barça, who twice levelled through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal, it represented their first loss of the season, bringing an end to their 11-game winning streak.

Both teams have big games to come in their respective leagues this weekend.

PSG face Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash in Ligue 1, while Barça host rivals Real Madrid in the Clásico.

articles.headline: How Raphinha's latest transformation made him into Barcelona's star striker
articles.description: Before Raphinha became Barcelona's captain and converted into their main striker, he was Premier League battling relegation at Leeds United. It was the making of him.
articles.headlineJa: ラフィニャの最新の変貌が、いかにして彼をバルセロナのスターストライカーへと変えたか
articles.descriptionJa: ラフィニャがバルセロナのキャプテンとなり、メインストライカーに転向する前、彼はリーズ・ユナイテッドでプレミアリーグの降格争いを繰り広げていた。それが彼を成長させた。
articles.body:
Raphinha's career has been characterized by constant change -- first, as he hopped between clubs in Brazil, Portugal, France, England and Spain. Recently, after settling in at Barcelona since 2022, the change has come in a different way: through coaches and his positioning on the pitch.

The Brazil international joined Xavi Hernández's Barça from Leeds United as a right winger, went on to excel on the left flank under Hansi Flick and is now delivering world-class performances this season as a No. 9, scoring 14 goals in 10 games going into Sunday's Clásico against Real Madrid (watch live at 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+).

It's perhaps no surprise to see him fulfilling so many different roles. Victor Orta, the sporting director who signed him for Leeds back in 2020, even imagined him playing in other positions.

- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Who has the stronger claim to win the Ballon d'Or?

- Tyler, The Creator joins list of music stars to appear on Barça Clásico kit

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

"I remember one day watching Vitória de Guimarães and thinking he could play as a wing back," Orta tells ESPN. "He had a different style to the typical, technical Brazilian. I said, 'Wow, he looks like he could run the 400 meters in athletics.'"

Raphinha will be 30 in December, and his path to the top of the game has not always been obvious. The 7-year-old who attended Ronaldinho's birthday party was not among the many Brazilian teenagers catapulted straight to one of Europe's elite clubs.

Instead, after fighting his way through várzea tournaments in his homeland -- dubbed by Raphinha himself as "the home of the rejects" -- he landed in Portugal with Vitória, going on to play for Sporting CP and then to French Ligue 1 club Stade Rennais. However, it was at Leeds, in the Premier League spotlight, where his career accelerated. 

Raphinha at Leeds

That is not to say it has been straightforward since. He was not always happy with his game time under former coach Xavi Hernández at Barça and thought he would leave the Spanish champions before Hansi Flick took over in 2024.

In Flick, he has found a manager whose style fits him superbly. The same could be said with Marcelo Bielsa at Leeds, although the Argentine coach wasn't convinced at first.

"Raphinha had been on our radar for a while, but the deal only became possible late in the transfer window," says Orta, now working at Spanish club Real Valladolid. "I was in the barbers one Saturday, very early, and I got a message from someone working with [Raphinha's then-agent, now Barça sporting director] Deco saying: 'Raphinha can leave because a new player is coming in.'

"I remember telling Marcelo. Perhaps because he didn't know him so well, the first reaction was: 'Do you know if he is good? Let me think...'

"But the market was closing. I told Marcelo to trust me. I remember he did some research, called me and said he had good opinions on the player. I said, 'OK, that's g

articles.headline: Alexis Mac Allister: 'Something wasn't right' under Arne Slot at Liverpool
articles.description: Alexis Mac Allister has said that Andoni Iraola fixed the issues within the Liverpool group left behind by his predecessor Arne Slot.
articles.headlineJa: アレクシス・マックアリスター：「アルネ・スロット体制下のリヴァプールでは、何かがうまくいっていなかった」
articles.descriptionJa: アレクシス・マックアリスターは、前任のアルネ・スロットが残したリヴァプール内部の問題を、アンドニ・イラオラが解決したと語った。
articles.body:
Alexis Mac Allister has said that Andoni Iraola fixed the issues within the Liverpool group left behind by his predecessor Arne Slot.

Slot won the Premier League in his first season in the Anfield dugout but Liverpool slumped to a fifth-place finish last campaign. The Dutchman was replaced by Iraola who oversaw a 4-3 Champions League win against Villareal on Tuesday night.

Mac Allister scored twice against Villareal before revealing the key changes Iraola has made since his arrival.

"Last year was a really difficult year for all of us," he told Amazon Prime. "It was clear that I was not at the level. I am the first one to say, I have no problem.

"Something wasn't right in the group. This manager changed it, and that's really important."

How has Iraola changed Liverpool tactics?

Mac Allister continued: "The way we play is quite different. I don't like to compare.

"I feel good, that's what I want and that's what I enjoy.

"Now, it's more man to man. You have to communicate less because you have to follow [the opponent]. Last year it was more of a zonal thing. With the national team we do more of a zonal thing and it works. Now, we do a one vs. one and it works.

"In the end, it's about us taking the responsibility.

"That's one of the changes. But now it's much easier, you have to think less but run more, maybe. That's the way football is going."

Liverpool fell behind to two early goals against Villareal but Mac Allister's header reduced the deficit.

"I am not tall! But I love going into the box," he said. "Coaches know that I like to attack the near post. I scored in the World Cup, as well. That's the place that I like to [get to].

"My dad is the same height, maybe a bit smaller, and he was good in the air as well."

After an equaliser from Ronald Araújo, Mac Allister's second goal was set up by Rio Ngumoha, who shone for Liverpool.

- Ngumoha sparks Liverpool's comeback Champions League win

- Rio Ngumoha revels in 'one of his best' performances after Anfield ovation

- Mac Allister, Ngumoha lead Liverpool rally to stay perfect in UCL

"Rio was amazing, he made the difference," Mac Allister said. "Sometimes you speak about players who score goals but he was really important.

"It is clear, the quality that he has. Everyone knows. It's easy to see that he is a really good player. He worked hard off the ball and that's important, as well."

The Argentina midfielder added: "The second goal; Rio, amazing, as well. I always speak with him about crossing the ball on the floor."

Florian Wirtz scored Liverpool's fourth before Villareal made it 4-3 through Tani Oluwaseyi.

articles.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama misses first 12 shots in rough opener vs. Thunder
articles.description: Victor Wembanyama didn't record his first bucket until the end of the third quarter and shot a career-worst 8% from the field as the Thunder got their revenge on the Spurs in Tuesday's Western Conference finals rematch.
articles.headlineJa: スパーズのヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマ、サンダー戦の開幕戦で序盤12本を外す苦戦
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日に行われた西カンファレンス決勝のリマッチで、サンダーがスパーズに雪辱を果たした。ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマは第3クォーター終了まで初得点を記録できず、フィールドゴール成功率はキャリアワーストの8%にとどまった。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- It took every bit of three quarters to do it, but Victor Wembanyama scrapped to earn his first bucket in Tuesday's 116-104 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Unfortunately for the San Antonio Spurs, it didn't come until the buzzer sounded to end the third quarter. Wembanyama fought through Chet Holmgren crossing half court, then set a screen on Cason Wallace before rolling to the basket for a spinning dunk off a lob from De'Aaron Fox. He missed his previous 12 shots up to that point, tying the mark for the second-most missed field goals to start a season opener in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98), according to Elias.

Wembanyama would finish the night shooting a career-worst 8% (1-for-13) from the field with 12 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks.

"I need to go back to playing the basketball I like," Wembanyama said. "This is not the sport I like right here. I've got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. I'm good when I have fun. I missed a lot of shots I usually don't miss. But after that, I didn't go back to these shots, and I wasn't decisive. I might be overthinking it. I don't need to do more. I need to think less probably."

Wembanyama shot 52.4% from the field last season in five regular-season games against Oklahoma City, averaging 18.4 points, as the Spurs rolled to a 4-1 record against the Thunder. In the Western Conference finals, Wembanyama boosted his scoring average against OKC to 27.3 points on 48.1% shooting from the floor.

Yet finding offensive success against the Thunder in Tuesday's opener proved much more difficult. Oklahoma City constantly showed the 22-year-old crowds while providing an optimal blend of help defense without letting San Antonio's other scorers loose.

Holmgren made up for a rough showing against Wembanyama in the Western Conference finals with an assertive, physical performance against him Tuesday and contributed 14 points and seven rebounds.

Holmgren swatted away a Wembanyama runner in the second quarter for one of his team-high four blocks. Rookie big man Aday Mara also logged a block against Wembanyama on a potential dunk off a Fox alley-oop. Isaiah Hartenstein chipped in, too.

"I thought he missed shots that he can normally make from the floor," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said of Wembanyama. "I thought Chet did a great job on him. I thought Mara did a great job on him in the possessions he had him. There's been times where we could get a little jumpy with him and we overhelp and give up something clean. There's other times where we've left him on an island. I thought tonight we had the perfect balance of providing help, putting him in a crowd, discipline on the ball, but not hemorrhaging in other parts of the floor."

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson declined to single out Wembanyama's shaky performance.

Oklahoma City jumped out to a 26-point lead in the second quarter, shooting a scorching 10-of-14 from 3-point range in the first half as San Antonio struggled to find it

articles.headline: Thunder win chippy opener vs. Spurs, throw support behind Chet Holmgren
articles.description: The scrap early in the second quarter of Tuesday night's season opener offered some symbolism for Chet Holmgren and his Thunder teammates. Holmgren landed with a thud. As he got back to his feet, his teammates had his back.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- The scrap early in the second quarter of Tuesday night's season opener offered some symbolism for Chet Holmgren and his Oklahoma City Thunder teammates.

Holmgren landed with a thud. As he got back to his feet, his teammates had his back.

That's how Holmgren's offseason went after his meek exit against Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference finals, which ended with a four-point, four-rebound dud from the All-NBA power forward/center in a Game 7 home loss. Holmgren opened this season with a strong performance in a 116-104 win over the Spurs, recording 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks and serving as the primary defender against Wembanyama, who struggled offensively, finishing 1-of-13 from the floor.

"Chet is an All-NBA talent on both ends of the floor," said Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who scored 32 points. "When he's himself, your team is better. It's as simple as that. When he's aggressive, when he's confident, when he's out there playing his game, he makes your basketball team better. It's no coincidence: He played better; we had a good night tonight. The box score doesn't show everything he does out there. He changes everything for us."

Holmgren's support from his teammates was displayed by their reaction to a flagrant foul 1 by Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox that left the lanky 7-footer sprawled on the floor in the middle of the paint. The other Thunder players on the floor converged to confront Fox. Four technical fouls were assessed after a review -- one on Wembanyama and one to each Williams on Oklahoma City's roster (Jaylin, Jalen and Kenrich).

"I'm going to get up and keep hooping, but I appreciate my teammates having my back," Holmgren said. "I'm not necessarily sure how exactly we get three techs for reactions to something else. I don't totally understand that.

"But at the end of the day, I feel like anything that you're not willing to reciprocate is an advantage for the other team. So if they want to play physical, we have to match that, and the refs are going to do their job in keeping that within the guidelines."

As Holmgren was posting up, Fox grabbed him by the shoulders from behind and tossed him to the floor. Fox implied that Holmgren embellished to sell the foul.

"[If] somebody grabs you like that and you go flying on the floor like that, you've got other problems to worry about," Fox said. "I didn't throw him that hard, I promise you."

The Thunder considered Fox's force on the play to be unnecessary and reacted accordingly, adding a bit of spice to what's shaping up to be the NBA's next great rivalry. Jaylin Williams was the first Thunder teammate to arrive on the scene, and he went face to chest with Wembanyama, who intervened on Fox's behalf. Jalen Williams and Kenrich Williams got in the mix a split-second after.

articles.headline: NFL chief medical officer: Eagles' approach to Hurts was 'appropriately guarded'
articles.description: At the owners meetings Tuesday in New York, NFL officials staunchly defended the process involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot issue, with chief medical officer Allen Sills addressing reporters in a media availability.
articles.headlineJa: NFLチーフ・メディカル・オフィサー：EaglesのHurtsへの対応は「適切に慎重であった」
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日にニューヨークで開催されたオーナー会議において、NFL関係者はフィラデルフィア・イーグルスのクォーターバック、ジェイレン・ハーツの血栓問題に関する一連のプロセスを強く擁護した。アレン・シルズ・チーフ・メディカル・オフィサーが記者会見で語った。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- NFL officials Tuesday staunchly defended the medical process involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot issue.

NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills was blunt in a news conference from the owners meetings.

"The notion that there's external factors that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way -- that's nonsense," Sills said.

The NFL is not punishing the Eagles for the handling of Hurts, who was cleared to play before Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after he was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf.

Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs days after the game.  Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for around three months.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs.

NFL officials confirmed Tuesday that it had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and Cleveland Clinic London throughout the process of Hurts being treated. Sills called the Eagles' treatment of Hurts "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

This week's news prompted rampant speculation about why the Eagles allowed Hurts to play in London.

Jeff Miller, NFL executive vice president overseeing player health and safety, called such speculation "considerable and uninformed," as well as "unfounded."

"Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts' health was always made the first priority and continues to be," Miller said.

The NFL declined to discuss specifics of Hurts' case, citing medical privacy. But Sills, who has been a team physical for three decades, said he has "tremendous confidence" in the Eagles' medical staff. The NFL works one to two years in advance of international games to prep for medical care, identifying local hospitals, physicians and resources at every site.

The medical experts tasked with evaluating players in such cases are not influenced by the team, Sills said.

"There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period," Sills said.

Doctors speculating online about "what should have been done" without all the data or being in the room with a patient are "unprofessional and unethical" in doing so, Sills said, citing a "sacred trust" between physicians and patients.

The NFL has tracked blood clot cases every season for the last decade and shares the data with the NFLPA, Sills said. Each year features a handful of cases.

"This isn't really a new situation, but it's something we examine," Sills said.

articles.headline: Steelers bring back veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling amid receiver injury woes
articles.description: The Steelers, in need of help at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson out because of injuries, signed veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling on Tuesday.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Marquez Valdes-Scantling is back with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Steelers signed the veteran wide receiver to their practice squad Tuesday ahead of a trip to Paris to take on the New Orleans Saints.

Valdes-Scantling, 32, spent a portion of the 2025 season in Pittsburgh, catching 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown in five games before adding three receptions in a first-round playoff loss to the Houston Texans.

Pittsburgh is in need of help at wide receiver after Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson were both put on injured reserve in the past week, leaving little experienced depth behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, who combined for 22 catches in a comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

The Steelers are Valdes-Scantling's third team in less than two months. He was released by the Dallas Cowboys in late August then signed with the Los Angeles Chargers in September, catching two passes for 22 yards in three games before being released last week.

Valdes-Scantling has a history with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers going back to their time together with the Green Bay Packers. Valdes-Scantling had 123 receptions in four seasons with the Packers from 2018 to 2021.

articles.headline: Commanders' Quinn, Daniels discuss QB's throwaway on fourth-down play
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's loss, coach Dan Quinn said.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズのクイン監督とダニエルズ、4ダウン目のスローアウェイについて語る
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダーズのダン・クイン監督は、月曜夜の敗戦における第2クォーター、QBジェイデン・ダニエルズが4ダウン目でパスをスローアウェイすべきではなかったと述べた。
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn said.

On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Daniels dropped back to pass and left the pocket after the 49ers started to generate pressure.

As Daniels ran to his right, two defenders pursued him, including linebacker Fred Warner. A flag was also thrown in front of Daniels. He could not make the first down running and with no open receiver in front of him he threw the ball away.

Quinn said he spoke to Daniels about the play.

"Even when you know there's a penalty, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it," Quinn said. "You don't know if it's gonna get picked up."

As it turned out the penalty wasn't an offsides call on the defense, which would have given Washington a first down. Rather it was an illegal shift on the Commanders.

"I didn't know. It could have been offside, it could have been on us," Daniels said if he anticipated an offsides call.

San Francisco declined the penalty because of the incompletion.

Daniels did complete 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. He helped Washington rally from a 20-3 halftime deficit and drove the Commanders deep into 49ers territory late in the game with a chance to take the lead.

"Like most things with him, there's some plays that you said, that's an incredible throw," Quinn said. "And there's other ones I'd love him to stay through the [read]."

He said he knew it would be tough for Daniels to gain yards scrambling because of the 49ers' team speed and their zone coverage with eyes on the quarterback. Indeed he rushed only four times for 10 yards.

Daniels was playing his second game wearing a brace on his left elbow that he dislocated in Week 2. Quinn said as Daniels evolves in coordinator David Blough's offense he'd like him to scramble more to throw. But he also knows he can make plays multiple ways.

"He always can make some throws that just kinda leaves you thinking, 'Man, there it is. There's only a few guys that can make that throw or that play,'" Quinn said.

articles.headline: Sources: Rams signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus
articles.description: The Rams, after releasing Harrison Mevis and an injury to Blake Grupe, are signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者発表：ラムズがフリーエージェントのキッカー、ブランドン・マクマナスと契約へ
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Networkが伝えた関係者の話によると、ラムズはハリソン・メビスの放出とブレイク・グルーペの負傷を受け、フリーエージェントのキッカーであるブランドン・マクマナスと契約する。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are signing kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday.

The Rams worked out McManus and free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday after kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL in a Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Grupe was playing in his first game for the Rams after he was signed to replace Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss.

McManus last kicked for the Green Bay Packers after signing with them in 2024. He was 44 of 51 for Green Bay over two seasons, with six misses coming during the 2025 season.

He spent his first nine seasons with the Denver Broncos and one with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was not on a roster to start the 2024 season while being investigated by the NFL for possible violations of the personal conduct policy. In September 2024, the NFL announced McManus was not in violation of the policy and he signed with the Packers three weeks later.
